source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Corvette Body, p.1B-33

procedures.title: Fractured panels
steps: File or grind the patch to the panel's general contour, taking care not to gouge the patch or nearby panel.
Fill any remaining flaws with plastic solder.
Let the fill harden, then finish sand ready for paint.

procedures.title: Panel replacement
steps: Cut out the damaged panel with a hacksaw blade, and clean all dirt and paint off the underside of the old panel(s) for about 2 to 3 inches back from the joint line.
Using lacquer solvent or equivalent, strip paint from the finish side of the adjoining panel for 2 to 3 inches next to where the new panel goes.
Scuff both the new panel and the adjoining panel for 2 to 3 inches back from the joint line, then wipe clean.
Bevel all mating edges to about 30 degrees through the full thickness so the joined pieces form a single V butt joint on the finish side; reshape the new panel if it does not fit the break closely.
Cut two backup pieces of woven glass fiber cloth running the full joint length (or shorter overlapping pieces), wide enough to lap the joint by 2 or 3 inches on each side.
Mix enough liquid plastic (resin with hardener) in an unwaxed paper cup (see Resin Repair procedure).
notes: Complete service panels, or sections cut from them, may be used (see Repair Panels in the general instructions). Fit the panel with all attaching parts installed to get correct alignment.
